question:
Which of the following optical devices can be used to produce a parallel beam of rays from a point source of light?

(A) Convex lens

(B) Concave lens

(C) Concave mirror

(D) Convex mirror
solution:
The correct answer is __**2 Only**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

To produce a parallel beam of rays from a point source of light, we need optical devices that can convert diverging rays from the point source into parallel rays. The following points explain why:

__
 
• **Convex Lens:** A convex lens can converge light rays from a point source to form a parallel beam if the point source is placed at its focal point. The rays emerging from the other side of the lens will be parallel to the principal axis.
 
• **Concave Mirror:** A concave mirror can also produce a parallel beam of rays if the point source is placed at its focal point. The reflected rays will be parallel to the principal axis.

**Why not the other options?**

 
• **Concave Lens:** A concave lens diverges light rays and cannot produce a parallel beam from a point source.
 
• **Convex Mirror:** A convex mirror also diverges light rays, making it unable to produce a parallel beam from a point source.

Therefore, the correct combination of optical devices that can produce a parallel beam of rays from a point source is both a convex lens and a concave mirror, which corresponds to **Option 2**__.
